verdict_text: YES. The script drops every `h.2.`, `h.5.`, `h.8.` tensor, maps the surviving old indices 0,1,3,4,6,7,9,10,11 to 0..8 in order via `enumerate(kept)`, and leaves the rest of each name and all tensor data untouched, so no collisions are possible since it writes into a fresh dict. Non-block tensors pass through unchanged. Before writing, it asserts the surviving block index set is exactly {0..8} (which also rules out any remaining block 9, 10 or 11 and enforces exactly 9 blocks) and that the total tensor count is 121; an assertion failure exits non-zero before `save_file`, so no output is written. The output goes to `out/T1/model.safetensors` as required.
